chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to Shurayh:
O Shurayh, do not speak privately with anyone in your court. And when you become angry, then stand up, and do not judge while you are angry.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The title of Imam Ali عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful.
key_terms.تَقْضِيَنَّ: You should not pass judgment or issue a judicial decision.
key_terms.تُسَارَّ: To speak privately or secretly with someone in a way that excludes others present.
key_terms.شُرَيْحٍ: Shurayh, the person being addressed in this instruction on judicial conduct.
key_terms.غَضِبْتَ: You became angry; entering a state of anger.
key_terms.غَضْبَانُ: Angry; in a state of anger that affects judgment.
key_terms.مَجْلِسِكَ: Your sitting place or court session where judgment is conducted.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali عليه السلام teach about judging while angry and private speech in court?
ai.summary: Imam Ali عليه السلام instructs Shurayh on the etiquette of judgment and judicial conduct. He forbids private side-conversations in the court setting and commands that judgment not be issued in a state of anger, emphasizing fairness, restraint, and proper decorum in governance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3239 - Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said to Shurayh:
"O Shurayh, do not speak privately with anyone in your court. And if you become angry, stand up and do not pass judgment while you are angry."
